title: Make your own HTML tag
summary: A custom element is an HTML tag you define.
introduction: A custom element is an HTML tag you define. Your task: Change the greeting words in connectedCallback.
learningObjectives: Change the greeting words in connectedCallback.
Explain the example for make your own html tag

blocks.text: A custom element is an HTML tag you define. Its name must contain a hyphen so it does not clash with built-in tags.
Run these HTML examples in this site's HTML playground. Each example defines its own custom element in a fresh page. No extra JavaScript library is needed.

blocks.code:
<hello-reader></hello-reader>
<script>
  class HelloReader extends HTMLElement {
    connectedCallback() { this.textContent = "Hello, reader!"; }
  }
  customElements.define("hello-reader", HelloReader);
</script>
blocks.title: Make your own HTML tag

blocks.text: Read the code step by step

items: `textContent` reads or replaces plain text inside an element. It does not interpret the supplied words as HTML.
`customElements.define` registers a hyphenated tag name with its class. Register a given name only once per document.
`connectedCallback` runs when the element joins the document. It can run again after a removal and reconnection.

blocks.text: The custom tag shows Hello, reader! after it is connected to the page.

blocks.title: A mistake to avoid
blocks.text: Register a tag name only once in a document. Use a hyphen in the name.

blocks.title: Your small task
blocks.text: Change the greeting words in connectedCallback.
